What is a tricopter and what is its main disadvantage?

A tricopter is a type of drone that can take off and land vertically and has six degrees of freedom on the X-Y-Z axes. Its cost is lower than other options. However, its important disadvantage is that it is not symmetrical.

Explain why a quadcopter is considered risky in case of a malfunction.

The quadcopter has four propellers and four motors, two on the right and two on the left, and its four-arm symmetrical structure gives it higher flight comfort. However, since the quadcopter system works as a whole, it has no backup plan or redundancy. Therefore, in case of any malfunction, the drone will most likely crash.

What load can a hexacopter and an octocopter each take off with?

A hexacopter can take off with a load of up to 10 kg, as in other models. An octocopter is an advanced type of drone that can take off with a load of 25 kg with its equipment, and it is especially preferred for heavily loaded works.

Why can't fixed-wing drones hover, and what do they need for launch and landing?

Fixed-wing drones use wings like a regular airplane instead of vertical lift rotors to provide lift, so they only need energy to move forward, making them more efficient for covering longer distances. The main disadvantage is that they cannot fly in one spot. Depending on their size, they need a runway or launcher to get into the air, and a runway, parachute, or net may be needed for a safe landing. Only the smallest fixed-wing drones are suitable for manual launch and belly landing in an open area.

Gasoline-powered fixed-wing drones can remain in the air for 16 hours or more.

Describe the fixed-wing hybrid VTOL drone category.

Fixed-wing hybrid VTOL drones are a new hybrid category that can also take off and land vertically, combining the advantages of fixed-wing UAVs with the ability to hover. These drones are a mix of fixed-wing drones with rotors attached to the blades and rotor-based drones. There are fixed-wing designs with no movement feature of vertical lift engines, models with motors that provide forward motion, and various types with propellers that can move up and down for takeoff and horizontally for forward flight.

According to payload, drones are divided into four classes: featherweight drones weigh less than 11 g with a load of 4-100 g and are mostly used for military surveillance; light drones weigh 200-1000 g with a payload of 150-270 g and are used in recreation and photography; medium-weight drones weigh 1-600 kg with a load of 400-1460 g; and heavy-lift aircraft weigh more than 160 kg with a payload of more than 1000 kg and are used in the cargo transport and cinema sector.

Drones by range are grouped as: very close range drones with a 5 km range and 1-hour flight time; close range drones with a 50 km range and 6-hour flight time; short-range drones with a 150 km range and 12-hour flight time; medium range drones with a 644 km range and 24-hour flight time; and long-range drones with more than 644 km range and more than 24-hour flight time. <think>I need to lay out battery, gasoline, hydrogen fuel cell, and solar power sources with their respective advantages and disadvantages as described in the source.</think>Drones are classified by power source as battery-powered, gasoline-powered, hydrogen fuel cell, and solar. Battery-operated drones are lightweight with sufficient energy storage and high discharge rates, but have disadvantages such as short lifespan, rapid energy consumption, and burn risks. Gasoline drones have advantages such as not needing expensive spare batteries and charging stations, no need to wait for recharging, high flight speeds, carrying heavy loads, and long flight times, but have undesirable features such as large size, noisy operation, and combustion and explosion risk due to fuel. Hydrogen fuel cell drones use renewable and environmentally friendly energy with higher energy efficiency than batteries, long flight time, and short refueling, but have disadvantages such as excessive heat generation and low operating efficiency. Solar drones have low operating costs and are lightweight but have limited flight time.

Explain the difference between brushed and brushless drone motors.

Brushed motors are the type used in recreational drones. Although inexpensive, they require much maintenance, and most are not in direct contact with the propeller. Brushless motors, being in connection with the rotor, reduce the need for maintenance and increase operating efficiency, and have much higher power. However, since brushless motors predominantly work with alternating current, each motor must have an electronic speed controller (ESC) that adjusts its rotation speed.

Describe the drone frame and list the most preferred frame models.

The drone body is the main skeleton system where all drone parts are placed, comparable to a computer chassis. It has an X-style design with four arms extending from the middle body, holding the rotors, battery, cards, and camera. F330, F450, and F550 models are the most preferred drone bodies, chosen for ease of spare parts supply, price/quality ratio, and performance. Despite its high price, the QAV250 fiber carbon body is also preferred because the carbon-fiber material reduces the possibility of breakage in case of falling.

How are drone batteries defined in terms of cells, and what voltage does each cell provide?

Drone batteries are defined as 1s, 2s, and 3s according to the number of cells in the battery. Each cell corresponds to a voltage of 3.7 volts. 1-cell lithium polymer batteries are preferred in light hobbyist drones, while 2- or 3-cell batteries are used in drones that require higher voltage.

What is the function of the flight control card in a drone?

The flight control card is the drone's brain. It is a circuit board that enables the UAV to move through the sensor information it receives, converting received signals into action for setting speed and direction, activating the camera, and executing other commands. By combining sensors such as the gyroscope, magnetometer, and accelerometer with GPS, flight control CPUs use data about the UAV's status, speed, position, and direction to guide flight and operation according to parameters set by the user before the flight.

What does the Power Distribution Board (PDB) do?

The PDB is a circuit board mounted on the drone that organizes the power connections of batteries, ESCs, and other onboard systems. It is unnecessary for all drones but helps create a neat and organized drone. In particular, it is responsible for power distribution from the flight battery to each electronic speed controller for the drone control board, and in some cases it is also used to power components such as the camera, LED taillights, and flight controller.

What is the role of the Electronic Speed Controller (ESC)?

The Electronic Speed Controller (ESC) is an essential part that only requires a little attention or maintenance, and its task is to control the speed of electronic motors. Each motor has its own ESC connection, and in many standard installations each branch has a separate ESC, though 4-in-1 ESC parts are also available. The ESC is the first place to look when a power-related problem occurs, especially local issues with a particular engine.

How many channels do drone receivers typically have and what do the four core channels control?

The receiver will have four channels to control the down, oscillation, acceleration, and yaw. However, many receivers have auxiliary channels to perform certain functions or trigger flight modes, and five or 6-channel receivers are generally the preferred models.

Explain the difference between CCD and CMOS camera sensors used in drones.

CCD sensors collect data using a scanning method for all pixels simultaneously. They have less jelly effect due to the global shot, high dynamic range performance, good performance in multi-light and low-light (WDR) environments, and better black/white transitions than CMOS. CMOS sensors collect line-by-line data for all pixels on the horizontal and vertical axis, which can create delays and may experience image distortions from the rolling shutter, known as the jelly effect. CMOS sensors have good color fidelity and performance, low power consumption, and are cheaper.

What two aspect ratios do drone cameras typically use, and how does field of view relate to angle?

Drone cameras have two aspect ratios, 16:9 and 4:3. Field of view (FOV) and angle are important user features: the larger the angle, the more difficult it is to view distant objects due to the fisheye appearance, while the smaller the field of view, the closer and clearer the image, which is preferred on immediate flights.

Generate a description of the Red Edge and Near-Infrared sensor bands used in drone imaging.

Red Edge is a band with a 717 nm center corresponding to a 12 nm bandwidth, which provides information on phytosterols and chlorophyll and is used in plant health, plant counting, and water management. Near-infrared (NIR) has an 842 nm center corresponding to a 57 nm bandwidth, and its reflection is used in soil and moisture analysis, crop health, and stress analysis depending on the chlorophyll level in the plant.

What is hyperspectral imaging used for on drones?

Hyperspectral imaging collects information and processes it across a wide part of the electromagnetic spectrum, beyond the three visible bands (red, green, and blue) the human eye detects, dividing the image into many bands. It can be used in the detection of underground resources in mining, agriculture, the prevention of diseases and pests, the military field, thermal infrared hyperspectral imaging, the chemical field for detecting colorless and odorless harmful substances in the air, environmental issues, and detecting leaking toxic wastes. Despite its wide-spectrum imaging advantages, it is very expensive and involves complex processing.

How do thermal cameras on drones create images, and what is one of their limitations?

Thermal imaging is based on invisible IR energy (heat), and thermal cameras make the image thanks to heat rather than light. Thermal cameras are used to map the amount of water in the soil (SWC) depending on the land surface temperature (LST). However, thermal cameras have limited spatial resolution, which often causes difficulties in homogeneous areas such as farmland with bare soil.

What sensors are used for obstacle detection and collision avoidance in drones?

Drones are equipped with collision avoidance systems consisting of sensors that detect obstacles. Data from the vision sensor, ultrasonic, infrared, LiDAR, time-of-flight (ToF), and monocular vision sensors transform images into 3D maps, allowing the flight controller to detect and avoid objects. With the help of software algorithms and SLAM technology using this data, 6-way obstacles are detected and necessary actions are taken to prevent them.

Define roll, pitch, and yaw as drone movement patterns.

Roll is the Z-axis on the nose and tail of the aircraft, i.e., longitudinal; it rotates around the axis and the wings move up and down. Pitch is the X-axis between one wing and the other wing of the aircraft, lateral; it rotates around the axis, meaning the nose and tail of the aircraft move up and down, also called the pitching motion. Yaw is the Y-axis that runs between the upper and lower parts of the fuselage, passing through the aircraft's center of gravity, meaning the rotational movement on the axis, or the right-left movement of the nose and wing of the aircraft.

What is the role of the gyroscope and IMU in drone flight stabilization?

The gyroscope immediately responds to varying forces coming into the drone by providing the necessary navigation information to the central flight controller. The inertial measurement unit (IMU) detects the current acceleration rate using the accelerometer and the gyroscope to see changes in rolling characteristics such as pitch, roll, and yaw. The IMU includes a magnetometer to calibrate against drift during flight. The gyroscope and IMU are core components of the drone flight controller, and gyro stabilization technology provides the drone with smooth flight capability using these components.

How does GPS ready-to-fly status get determined, and what are no-fly zones?

According to the compass calibration, when the drone starts to work, it searches for the position of GPS satellites; when more than six satellites are detected, the drone becomes ready-to-fly. To increase flight safety and prevent accidents in restricted areas, the no-fly zone feature is activated and flight is blocked. No-fly zones are divided into two categories, A and B, and these regions can be renewed and changed by software updates.

What is Time-of-Flight (ToF) technology and what does it enable?

Time-of-Flight (ToF) is a precision mapping and 3D imaging technology that emits a very short pulse of infrared light and measures the rotation time of each camera sensor pixel. Flash LiDAR time-of-flight cameras offer solutions by measuring distances within a captured scene, making operations such as object scanning, obstacle avoidance, tracking and recognizing objects, and measuring volumes easier.

Drones are successfully used in environmental control and emergency response processes. To prevent environmental pollution, drones carry out projects aimed at cleaning the seas and make an important contribution to the fight against poaching and the tracking of endangered animals, with behavior and disease conditions of animals followed thanks to thermal cameras. Oil companies also use drones for inspections of oil and gas leaks, with thermal cameras performing important tasks in detecting leaks quickly and preventing possible risks.

Professional video shoots are made today using drones in commercials, TV series, and movie sets, successfully capturing specific images. What challenges exist in using drones for logistics?

Drones are used in the logistics industry to transport food, packages, or goods, and are preferred for transporting urgent or frequently sent small parcels and for delivery to hard-to-reach areas. One of the most important and pending problems in logistics use is that drones need sufficient carrying capacity. Heavy-duty drones can improve road traffic by replacing existing carriers for material management and transporting goods between warehouses.

How are drones used in emergency response situations?

Drones help the fire brigade, police officers, volunteer rescuers, and more in emergencies. They are used for reconnaissance before guiding the rescue team, especially when the extent of the disaster is unknown. Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) prevent possible drownings and assist in rescue in situations such as when a boat capsizes, and drones are also used to search for the injured in avalanche cases.

How do drones contribute to wildlife conservation and reforestation?

Drones are an economical and effective alternative to monitor wildlife species and protect natural life. Rapid aerial observations help gain a better idea of the health of the species and ecosystem, monitor and research migration routes by monitoring animal groups, and prevent poaching. Drones also scan forest floors destroyed by fires, releasing seed containers containing seeds, fertilizers, and nutrients to help trees regenerate, which is important given that reforestation with human labor alone would take many years.

What are the two main barriers to widespread drone technology adoption?

The two main barriers summarized are power source and security. For power source, the limited flight times mean developing drones capable of long flights with smaller and more powerful batteries remains a priority, along with systems that can analyze terrain with object detection software instead of heavier onboard systems. For security, the risks include falling due to limited battery power and fast spinning propellers, the need for permits in residential areas, obstacle detection technology to prevent accidents, and law enforcement to limit interference with others' privacy, as well as the growing risk of cyberattacks where hackers can intercept transmitted data to take control of the drone.

In the UK, the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) limits the flight altitude of unmanned aerial vehicles to 500 feet for drones weighing more than half a kilo, and it is important to register with the CAA. It is prohibited to fly near airports, and under the Dronecode it is mandatory to stay below 400 feet and at least 150 feet away from buildings and people, with the drone constantly observed during flight.

Conditions for Fall: mg > Feq, All moments = 0

- Fixed-Wing UAVs: winged pilotless aircraft with actuators like ailerons, elevators, and rudder similar to a small airplane. Designed to cover longer distances and carry heavier payloads, but require a launch mechanism and runway since they lack VTOL capability.
- Multi-copter/Multi-rotor: aircraft lifted and propelled by multiple horizontal rotors. Mostly used for short-duration flights over shorter distances, consuming more energy since they can't glide like fixed-wing UAVs.
